content:
Facts – A granddaughter challenged a holographic will, alleging lack of autography and heterography because the testamentary text was written in block capital letters, while the signature was cursive.
Legal framework – Arts. 602 and 606 Italian Civil Code; rules on authenticity of holographic wills; burden of proof in negative declaration actions.
Issue – Whether a holographic will written in block letters, but signed by the testator, lacks the handwritten requirement and is therefore null.
Principles applied – The Court held that the burden of proving non-authorship lies with the party contesting the will. The handwritten requirement under Art. 602 ICC does not impose any specific graphic style, as block letters are not excluded per se. Autography depends on the referability of the entire document to the testator, regardless of character type. The use of block letters is a factual element relevant only for evidentiary assessment, not a formal validity requirement. Where graphological analysis, comparative writings of certain origin, and witness evidence demonstrate habitual use of block letters by the testator, the will is valid. Nullity arises only when even a single part of the testamentary text is written by a third party, which was excluded in the present case.
